scope: Shared reader vocabulary for Objais revenue and acquisition, covering current scope and future options

terms.definition: One person whose possessions are being considered. Three watches and a car still count as one owner; a representative acting for them is not an extra owner.

In the consumer revenue examples, the asset owner using Objais, including someone using it for free. The insurer or broker paying a lead fee has a different role; a future professional offer would need its own account unit.
Someone authorised to act for an owner, such as a staff member or adviser.
Bringing a new owner into the measured service.

Total attributable cost of bringing in new owners, divided by the number of distinct newly acquired owners. Include advertising, introduction fees and onboarding work; clicks, installs and returning owners do not automatically add to that denominator.
The route that brings someone in, such as an advertisement or a dealer introduction.
A distinct person reached before they join the service.
The share of prospects who join the measured service.
A person or organisation participating in the service, such as an owner, representative, Objais or an insurer. Roles explain who acts and who pays; they are not interchangeable counting units.
An agreed payment to Objais when a service introduction meets its payment condition.
A possible transaction that could earn Objais a fee.

An occurrence that meets the agreement’s condition for earning an Objais fee. Both guides also call this a payable event. The fee may be earned before cash arrives, and the contract determines whether acceptance, policy binding or another occurrence qualifies.
An insurance enquiry passed to a partner.
An enquiry that meets the agreed requirements.
A lead accepted as payable under the partner agreement. “Paid” describes the entitlement to the fee in these examples; it does not establish that money has already arrived.
An owner with an opportunity that can still earn its first fee.
The chance that an active eligible owner needs help in the month being modelled. The symbol is n; need can depend on season or time since acquisition.
The chance of a qualified request, given that an active eligible owner needs help. The symbol is p. This is a conditional rate, not a share of all visitors.
The chance that a qualified request meets the contractual payment condition. The symbol is α (alpha). Under a binding arrangement, the condition is effective cover rather than lead acceptance.

The monthly chance of an active eligible owner reaching the initial payable event: q = n × p × α. Payment-history rules and delivery capacity may reduce realised events further. Click-to-request and request-to-payment yields have different denominators.
terms.original_revenue_term: Conversion probability, q = n × p × α

terms.definition: The contract providing insurance cover.
The point when insurance cover becomes effective under its contract. A quotation or accepted enquiry does not by itself establish effective cover.
The price of the insurance.
The agreed payment for arranging the cover.
The amount Objais has earned.
A fee withdrawn or credited back.
A request for payment.
An amount earned and still awaiting payment.
Money actually received.
Costs that change with the people served or work done, such as service and processing expenses.
Expenses assumed to stay the same within the volume being considered, such as the monthly overhead used later in this guide.
Revenue minus variable costs and acquisition costs. Fixed costs have not yet been deducted.
The point where the stated result reaches zero. Owner contribution, company operating result and cash result have different break-even conditions; always name the result and period.

A group followed from a stated entry period or experiment. The revenue guide groups distinct owners by acquisition month; the acquisition guide can follow linked entry journeys. State the counting unit and entry rule before comparing cohorts.

Continuation in a specified relationship over time. App use, an active opportunity, insurance cover and software billing each need their own measure; continuation in one does not prove continuation in another.
An active owner whose current opportunity has not yet earned its initial payment. Payment history and capacity still determine whether an event can occur this month.
An active owner whose current opportunity has earned its initial payment. Continued use alone cannot earn that same fee again.
Owners who have gone quiet but may return, retaining the unpaid or paid status of their opportunity. Return preserves owner identity and payment history.
The opportunity relationship has ended in the model. This does not automatically end a policy or software billing relationship.
The share remaining in the opportunity relationship next month. It can differ before and after payment.
The share of continuing monetised owners who gain a genuinely new eligible opportunity. The symbol is λ (lambda). Another item or return visit qualifies only when the agreement supports a new fee.
One owner served for one month.
Giving money earned later less weight than money earned now when comparing amounts across time.

terms.term: Customer contribution over a stated horizon
terms.definition: Discounted revenue less variable and acquisition costs, per originally acquired owner over the stated period. The guide normally uses 36 months and a 1% monthly discount rate. Fixed costs are excluded.
A limit on initial paid events for each owner over every consecutive window, such as two events in any 12 months.
A minimum gap between initial paid events, such as six months.
A software service sold for a recurring payment.
The record of that billing relationship.
What Objais retains after payment fees or partner shares, before service costs.
The share of paid accounts still paying next month.
The share of paid accounts whose payments stop.
The share of policies still in force each month.
Continuing insurance cover for another term.
The contractual right for Objais to receive a payment when a policy renews.
The difference between two percentage rates. Moving from 95% to 96% is one percentage point; it is not a 1% relative increase.
The relationship between the number of prospects reached and the cost of reaching them. In this model, a rising curve makes additional prospects more expensive.
An assumed or measured factor that changes prospect costs over time to represent cost pressure.
Revenue less variable, acquisition and fixed costs during the calendar period being considered.
Money received minus expenses paid during that period.

The cash shortfall that needs financing when expenses fall due before enough receipts arrive. The largest shortfall can occur before the end of the forecast, even if the final cash balance is positive.
Based on actual records.
Supported by an agreement or other written evidence.
Chosen to explore a possibility.
The evidence is still missing.
Paid messages or placements that bring people toward the service. Compare their downstream outcomes as well as their reach.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: A sequence connecting arrival, a useful task, a request and a commercial outcome. Different entry routes may have different steps while reaching comparable payment conditions.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md
terms.source_heading: The customer journey and commercial funnel

terms.definition: A measure used to understand an outcome or diagnose a stage of the journey. Each metric needs a counting unit, denominator, period and source.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: The first useful product result under a stated rule, such as obtaining a usable estimate in the proposed photo journey. This product milestone is separate from activation of insurance cover.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md
terms.source_heading: The customer journey and commercial funnel

terms.definition: Evidence that someone wants the offered help, such as a request for a personalised quotation. Interest in trying a feature alone does not establish insurance intent.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md
terms.source_heading: The customer journey and commercial funnel

terms.definition: Checking whether a request meets the relevant country, asset and service requirements. The criteria must be stated; a qualified request is not automatically payable.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md
terms.source_heading: The customer journey and commercial funnel

terms.definition: One appearance of an advertisement in platform reporting. Several impressions can belong to the same person.
Outbound link clicks divided by impressions for the same platform and period. The example’s 1,000 clicks from 20,000 impressions give 5%; other definitions of “click” would change the measure.
Media spend divided by outbound clicks in the stated campaign and period. It measures advertising cost per click, not the full cost per acquired owner.
Media spend divided by impressions, multiplied by 1,000. Keep the platform, reporting period and currency consistent.

The share reaching a payable event from a named starting group. Twenty-five payable events mean 50% of 50 submissions, 62.5% of 40 qualified requests, or 2.5% of 1,000 entry clicks; these rates cannot be substituted for one another.

Cost divided by the number of a named outcome, such as submitted requests or payable events. State the cost scope: a media-only CPA excludes introduction and onboarding costs. Owner CAC uses full attributable costs and distinct new owners.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md
terms.source_heading: Translate the funnel into acquisition limits

terms.definition: Attributable revenue divided by advertising spend. These examples use Objais fees after expected reversals, not premiums or asset values. A ratio above one can still leave a loss after delivery costs.

The underlying platform, such as WhatsApp or Facebook. One network can host many separate communities. This community meaning is different from an advertising network that buys media across publishers.
terms.source_heading: Separate the network from the community and its organiser

terms.definition: A particular group using a network. Membership does not establish that someone saw an invitation or became an Objais owner.
terms.source_heading: Separate the network from the community and its organiser

terms.definition: The person or business organising a community or its activity, such as an administrator, store or auction host. An operator may run several groups and is a different role from the owner of a collectible.
terms.source_heading: Separate the network from the community and its organiser

terms.definition: A listing, auction, sale, exchange, shipment or collection update that creates a possible task need. It does not automatically earn Objais a fee.
terms.source_heading: Separate the network from the community and its organiser

terms.definition: A game using collectible trading cards. In these guides, TCG identifies a possible collection and community market; it does not establish Objais recognition capability, insurance availability or paid demand.
terms.source_heading: Match the offer to the moment

terms.definition: What it takes for a person to complete their task and understand the result: effort, errors, recovery and confidence, including any partner handoff.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: Whether the intended task is completed correctly under a stated rule. Finishing screens quickly does not establish that the result is understood.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: Time from a defined start to the first useful result. For the proposed photo journey, that result could be a usable estimate; it is not the time until insurance cover begins.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: Whether a person understands the result, checked against a stated question or criterion. In the proposed research, owners explain the estimate in their own words.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: Elapsed time between a defined start and result. State the attempts included; report failures separately rather than making them disappear from performance results.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: The middle value of ordered observations, also called the 50th percentile. For completed-attempt times, it describes a typical completion; failed attempts still need their own count.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: A value at or below which 95% of the measured observations fall. For completed-attempt latency, it describes the slower tail; it does not account for excluded failures.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: A cohort that has had the agreed observation window. Maturity does not make every request resolved: show pending outcomes and their ages separately.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: Separating results by meaningful differences, such as country, asset, channel, partner, device or acquisition period. Small groups may still be too uncertain to compare reliably.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: A recorded occurrence, such as a request submission or fee being earned. A product event or commerce event is not necessarily a payable event.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: Checking that product, partner and finance records agree about the same underlying opportunities and fees. It helps expose retries, duplicates and mismatched decisions.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: Assigning credit for an outcome to a channel or interaction under a stated rule. Several platforms can claim the same outcome; their claims do not create several underlying fees.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: The additional activity caused by an intervention, such as an advertisement. Assigning channel credit alone cannot establish this effect.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: A comparison group not exposed to the intervention being studied. A credible comparison can help estimate its additional effect; a small pilot may support only a directional conclusion.
terms.source: Objais Funnels Advertising Metrics and UX Research.md

terms.definition: Collectible cards used in games or collected for subjects such as sports. Trading card games (TCGs) are one part of this market; sports cards need their own demand and service assumptions.
terms.source_heading: Trading card games and sports cards

terms.definition: A service connecting advertisers with space across participating publishers’ websites or apps. This is a media-buying route, distinct from a community platform such as WhatsApp.
The ad space a publisher or network makes available to buy. A large or relevant audience does not establish that this space is offered to outside advertisers.
The particular banner, feed item, app surface or sponsored message where an advertisement appears. Availability depends on the publisher, country, format and offer.

commercial_gaps: Actual contractual payment conditions and renewal rights
Observed need, return, conversion and adoption rates
Full attributable costs, distinct identities and collection dates
Future paid demand, professional account units and country-specific availability
